sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: PCT Patent Application and International Trademark Registration

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (metropolitan and overseas, single national corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification, unitary national system, commercial company law via Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Double Taxation Convention (1984, amended by 2013 Protocol)
France-United States Income Tax Convention (1994, as amended by PAB 2006)
France-Germany Double Taxation Convention (1959, as amended 2015)
European Patent Convention (EPC, 1973, revised 2000) and Implementation Regulation applicable to patent prosecution
Unified Patent Court Agreement (UPC Agreement, in force 1 June 2023)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; ratification suspended; not in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations for obliged entities); Décret n° 2021-1626 of 14 December 2021 (UBO register filing requirements); Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed; Code de commerce Articles L.561-45 to L.561-49 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE); Ordonnance n° 2021-1657 of 15 December 2021 and Décret n° 2022-404 of 21 March 2022 governing the regulated profession of Conseil en Propriété Industrielle (CPI) as a reporting professional; Loi n° 2016-1691 (Sapin II) for transparency and anti-corruption.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (access restricted to Tracfin, judicial authorities, ACPR, banks and other AML-obliged entities; public access to the French UBO register is not available following CJEU jurisprudence restricting AMLD5 public disclosure)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of association (Statuts) of the SARL, including share transfer clauses and governance provisions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary (notaire) or private lawyers acting under legal attestation (authentication of statutory signatures); notarized act required when contributions include immovable property or benefits in kind
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic French notarial act requiring no apostille for French internal registration; foreign shareholders' signatures consular legalization or Hague Apostille in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of identification documents and proof of address for all shareholders and the nominated manager (Gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuing state authority (passport office, municipal registry) with certified translation by a sworn French translator (traducteur assermenté)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the shareholder's jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the local French Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record certificate / certification of non-bankruptcy and legal capacity for the Gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the Gérant's country of residence; French authorities issue the official « bulletin n° 3 du casier judiciaire »
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization when issued abroad; domestic French certificate requires no external legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of share capital deposit (Attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by a French licensed credit institution or regulated payment services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French bank or regulated fintech holding the SARL's blocked share capital account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal French banking certificate, no apostille required; if issuer is a foreign branch, apostille and French sworn translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Regulated domiciliation agreement (Contrat de domiciliation) covering the SARL's registered office or proof of ownership/lease of the business premises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office domiciliation company (gestionnaire de domiciliation) or the lessor/notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic French contract; no apostille required, but the domiciliation company must be certified under CMF/Code de commerce provisions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and sanctions screening against: (a) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (FInD); (b) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists (Al-Qaida ISIL List under resolution 2253, Taliban list under resolution 1988); (c) French national freezing measures published by Tracfin and the French Directorate General of the Treasury; (d) OFAC SDN List recommended where USD transactions or US-nexus services are used; (e) French domestic terrorist asset freezes under CMF Articles L.562-1 to L.562-15. Enhanced due diligence required for high-risk third-country nationals, shell structures, and non-face-to-face incorporation. Continuous monitoring obligation at onboarding and on any event triggering review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Formalités des entreprises — Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) as registrar of the Registre national du commerce et des sociétés (RNCS); search interface for mark conflict and company name availability available via data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language mandatory for the statutory name under the Loi Toubon (Law n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994). The corporate name must be in Latin script with French orthography and accentuation; standard French company-name endings (SARL, EURL) must appear. Latin transliteration of a French name is not permitted for the registered legal name; where the founding shareholder uses a non-Latin alphabet, the share register, articles and corporate books must carry a certified French transliteration. Intellectual property and patent agency service marks may additionally use English for the trade name, but the legal name must remain French-regulated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a formal name-reservation system; the 30-day window represents the statutory publication and opposition observation period for a newly incorporated entity (registration notice published in a legal announcements journal and the applied entity name reported to the RCS). If the greffe (court registry under the INPI/Guichet unique process) rejects the name on grounds of confusion with an existing corporate name or prior trademark, the applicant must file a written demand for the registry's detailed statement of reasons. A corrective re-filing through the Guichet unique may be made within 30 days using a modified identifier. Where the rejection is maintained, an appeal may be filed with the President of the competent commercial court (Tribunal de commerce) via the expedited procedure (référé) within 15 days of receipt of the formal refusal; alternatively, if the conflict arises from a prior national or EU trademark, the applicant may institute trademark nullity proceedings or negotiate a coexistence consent before the relevant court or INPI, whichever is applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a regulated commercial domiciliation agent (gestionnaire de domiciliation) under Articles L.123-11-2 to L.123-13 of the Code de commerce, subject to declaration of the domiciliation contract in the RCS file and use of a physical 'local d'affaires'. A wholly virtual office is not considered commercially sufficient for an ISIC 7490 patent and trademark prosecution agency because professional activity as a Conseil en Propriété Industrielle requires verifiable professional premises, insurance, confidentiality infrastructure, and records access. Nevertheless, a virtual registered address is acceptable for the SARL's legal seat, provided that the operational address of the patent attorneys is separately disclosed to Tracfin, the INPI professional register, and clients.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Quantified estimate of 15% cumulative probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by Tracfin, the regional business inspection unit, or the INPI professional oversight body within the first three years of operations. Probability increases to approximately 35% if the company fails to file accurate UBO declarations, if the domiciliation address is flagged as a high-risk shell address, or upon any customer complaint regarding patent prosecution fraud.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and civil-law review of the SARL articles of association (statuts) by a French business attorney, including share transfer, governance and dissolution clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed fee of approximately EUR 1,300-1,800; statutory tariff not fixed for avocat drafting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of foreign shareholders' incorporation documents, passports, UBO disclosures and powers of attorney into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-registered translator customary fee of EUR 0.40-0.80 per word or EUR 25-45 per document page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of foreign origin documents (shareholders' certificates, criminal records, corporate registries)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent receiving authority in the shareholder's country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated apostille authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed government tariff; USD 20-40 per document in most contracting states; consular legalization up to USD 150 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication notice (avis de constitution) in a legal announcements journal (Support d'annonces légales — ALO) and the service of the Directors' certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal announcements newspaper (ALO) approved in the commercial court department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory-controlled tariff of approximately EUR 190 for a standard SARL incorporation announcement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee payable to the commercial court registry (greffe) through the Guichet unique, including the UBO declaration file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (RCS) via INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated registry tariff of approximately EUR 82 (includes IRC bond fee and corporate registration fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration as a regulated professional council in Intellectual Property (Conseil en propriété industrielle) or inscription of the SARL in the CPI professional register, including proof of professional indemnity insurance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) and the CPI professional order
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual practice right and register inscription fee of approximately EUR 900-1,200 for a one- to two-license practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Year one regulated office domiciliation contract (first year) at a commercial address in Paris or Lyon
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market monthly fee of EUR 20-60; this item covers EUR 290 for a cost-effective compliant offer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of a professional business bank account and certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) at a licensed French bank or regulated fintech
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or payment services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Issuance fee of EUR 150-250 plus account activation; standard for low-risk professional services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for notary fees in case of contributions in kind, lease agreement takeover or if notarized articles are required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff; in-kind contribution certification often EUR 700-1,200; no charge if not activated (this is provided as optional buffer)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tracfin-compliant UBO and PEP screening system setup and ongoing monitoring subscription for the patent agency's client onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/KYC software vendor or compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual subscription; EUR 250-600 for SME-grade screening and adverse-media monitoring

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq.; Civil Code Article 1832; Order No. 2023-489 on the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (or Tribunal Judiciaire) in the territorial jurisdiction of the SARL's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) and a Déclaration de constitution de société (form M0), filed electronically via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The share capital is freely fixed (minimum €1). Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (bank, Caisse des Dépôts, or notary) before filing; at least 20% of each cash contribution must be paid up upon incorporation, the residual within 5 years. In-kind contributions must be fully released upon signature. The escrow deposits are released only after the company obtains its K-bis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constitutive meeting of the shareholders of the Company, held at the fixed registered office, the subscribers, acting as sole members under Article L.223-18 of the French Commercial Code, resolve: First, the articles of association are adopted unchanged. Second, the share subscription list, signed by each subscriber, is approved and the allocation of quotas to each shareholder is ratified. Third, the registered office is fixed at the address set in the articles, which shall serve as the legal and administrative seat. Fourth, the shareholders jointly appoint the designated Manager as first gérant, with full powers to bind the company in ordinary operations. This resolution is adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders; optionally a notary public for notarially authenticated deeds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in compliance with Article L.223-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce. Include the corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, corporate purpose (PCT patent prosecution and international trademark registration), duration (up to 99 years), share capital, nominal value and allocation of quotas, transfer restrictions, identity of the gérant, and any in-kind contribution valuations. All quotas must be subscribed. Each shareholder signs the statuts or executes a notarized deed; if signing by proxy, a legalized power of attorney is annexed.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney (if signed by proxy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later rejects the statuts for non-conforming clauses, convene a general meeting to amend the statuts or obtain a unanimous written decision, and file a rectified version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Obtaining Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; alternatively a notary acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'compte de dépôt de fonds pour constitution de société' in the company's name. Deposit the cash contributions into this blocked account by transfer or deposit. The depositary issues a 'certificat du dépositaire des fonds' stating the amount and account details. For in-kind contributions, arrange a contribution auditor's report if required by Article L.223-9. The funds must remain blocked until the company is registered in the RCS and the K-bis is issued.
required_dossiers: Appraiser's report for in-kind contributions (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate is denied due to identity discrepancies, correct the shareholder/managers' personal data and obtain a revised certificate; if the capital is incomplete, place supplemental funds and re-request certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved legal announcements journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the avis de constitution including the company name, 'SARL', registered office address, share capital, corporate object, duration, manager's identity, and the intended RCS Registry. Submit it to the chosen JAL online or via a legal process server. Obtain an attestation de publication or the original journal issue after publication. The notice must be published before the Guichet Unique filing.
required_dossiers: Proof of publication (attestation or original journal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a JAL is not approved or the notice is defective, choose an approved journal and publish a corrected notice; any erroneous data is cured through addendum publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique, select 'Création d'une personne morale', and complete the M0 declaration with the company's identifiers, managers, shareholders, share distribution, and the relevant French activity code corresponding to ISIC 7490. Upload PDF scans of the signed statuts, bank certificate, publication proof, declaration of beneficial owner, addresses, and identity documents. Submit the dossier. The Guichet forwards it to the competent Greffe and confirms a filing timestamp.
required_dossiers: Declaration of beneficial owner (Article L.561-2-2 du Code monétaire et financier)
Copy of passport/ID of the manager(s) and all shareholders
Proof of registered office address (lease or domiciliation contract)
Power of attorney for the filing intermediary (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet sends a completeness query or request for correction, rectify the missing items within 30 days through the same portal. A legalized signature or clarification may be added without re-doing the whole filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with RCS and Issuance of K-bis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Tribunal Judiciaire - Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the complete dossier, the legality of the statuts, and the regularity of formalities. Upon approval, it registers the company in the RCS, allocates a SIREN number, and produces the official K-bis extract. The K-bis contains the company's identity, registered office, legal form, directors, and registration details. The applicant receives the K-bis via the Guichet or post. Payment of the droit de greffe and ancillary taxes is required prior to issuance.
required_dossiers: Payment of official registration fees as set by the Greffe
Any requested supplementary evidence (e.g., additional notarial certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe suspends or refuses registration, the applicant is invited to remedy defects within a legal delay. An appeal may be filed with the President of the competent commercial court under Article L.123-5-2 of the Code de commerce in cases of unjustified refusal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — portal: impots.gouv.fr; business formalities via guichet-unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: (1) incorporate via the Guichet Unique to obtain SIREN/SIRET, Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, and RBE filing; (2) automatically obtain a VAT intracommunautaire (TVA) number from DGFiP when the entity is liable for French VAT; for a non-resident entity without French establishment, register through the French VAT department (SIE) and appoint a fiscal representative for VAT purposes if required; (3) open a professional tax space on impots.gouv.fr for filing CIT and VAT; (4) for EU distance sales or OSS use, register on the One-Stop-Shop portal; (5) for import/export operations, obtain an EORI number via DGFiP/douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS); restricted pass-through election exists for qualifying small/family SARLs under specific statutory provisions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box system. Available elections: (a) option for transparent partnership taxation (impôt sur le revenu) for small SARL de famille or under Article 239bis AA CGI for the initial tax years; (b) option for VAT consolidation (assujetti unique) to treat France group entities as a single taxable person; (c) option to designate a permanent establishment for VAT purposes and for services place-of-supply reverse charge mechanisms; (d) notification and documentation requirements for hybrid mismatch transparency under ATAD/Article 212 bis CGI; all elections must be filed with DGFiP and maintained in tax records.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Article 293 B CGI: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for supplies of goods and certain services; EUR 37,500 for taxable services (excluding goods), including patent and IP services; for EU cross-border distance sales of goods and B2C digital/remote services, an EU-wide EUR 10,000 registration threshold applies through the OSS scheme; foreign suppliers without a permanent establishment are generally required to register in France from the first French taxable supply absent applicable simplification.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing in France is being phased in (large enterprises from 1 September 2026; small/medium enterprises from 1 September 2027) through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), with API integration via PDP partners. Invoices must be issued in structured electronic format (Factur-X / PEPPOL BIS / UBL) and e-reporting of B2C/intra-EU transactions is required; there is no real-time digital stamping system, but fiscal clearance occurs through the PPF receiving workflow and obligations for archiving, invoice integrity, and TVA identification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the EU are eligible for 0% VAT (French TVA exonération) where the exporter holds custody of the goods, the goods leave the EU under customs supervision, and proof of export is retained (Article 262 CGI). For the patent prosecution agency's cross-border services, French VAT does not apply if the recipient is a taxable business established outside the EU (B2B place-of-supply rule under Article 259-1 CGI), or if the services are treated as physically performed outside France; the supplier must document the non-EU business status and the recipient's country of establishment. Services supplied to non-business persons or relating to French immovable property remain taxable under French VAT rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (C21/DELTA+G) accepted and stamped by French customs (Déclaration d'Exportation)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR or other contract of carriage evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank FX receipt matching export proceeds
For services: written contract, invoice, evidence of professional performance of services, and, where requested, certificate of tax residence of the non-EU invoice recipient
EORI number and proof of status of the exporting entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may re-assess inaccurate export zero-rating within the general three-year statute of limitations, extended to six years in deliberate tax fraud cases and ten years in certain cross-border concealment scenarios. An unjustified 0% VAT export invoice or unlawful VAT refund is clawed back with statutory interest (0.2% per month, i.e., approximately 2.4% p.a.) plus penalties of 40% for intentional misstatement or 80% for fraudulent abuse/opposition to tax control. Criminal exposure includes fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment (five years), disqualification from public procurement, and joint liability of the managing director in the SARL.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full capital account convertibility and current account convertibility under EU regulations and the Monetary and Financial Code. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permitted without prior approval, subject only to standard tax reporting and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service exports including PCT patent applications and international trademark registration, no mandatory surrender of proceeds is required. Invoices are issued in EUR and funds credited directly to corporate accounts. Mandatory surrender applies solely to goods exports, typically within 90 days at official rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility with regulated fintech EMI providers such as Wise, Revolut Business and N26 Business. Legal constraints include French AML/CFT compliance, potential licensing requirements for cross-border transfers and restrictions on offshore accounts for certain corporate activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC is permitted for standard SARL accounts via Banque de France-approved digital platforms. Directors and beneficial owners must appear physically for initial onboarding of accounts exceeding defined thresholds or for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening failure or adverse media exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of clean background, source of funds statements and beneficial ownership certificates from official registries
Updated articles of association, shareholder agreements and notarized declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols utilize SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose codes such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SERVICE FEES'. Verification requires matching client invoices, KYC documentation and beneficial ownership proofs. For French SARL, use of local IBAN accounts with BIC code is mandatory for domestic clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for international payments, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 and SEPA Instant for eurozone transfers. Patent-related disbursements such as attorney fees are routed through correspondent banking networks with proper purpose codes to avoid regulatory flags.

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés); reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; a reduced 10% patent-box effective rate applies to net qualifying intellectual property licensing income of approved patent assets.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box: 10% reduced corporate income tax rate on net income from qualifying patent inventions and connected IP licenses, subject to election and strict substance, development, and acquisition-cost conditions. SME reduced rate: 15% on first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit where the company meets the French SME definition. R&D tax credit: 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that amount. Tax losses may be carried forward under the general regime, subject to an annual deduction ceiling of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit above that threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultat) and mandatory annex schedules 2050-A/B/F/G/H, 2051, 2052, 2053, 2058-A/B; mandatory professional electronic filing through the impots.gouv.fr platform using the EFI/EDI channel, with transmission through a partner EDI account or the État facteur identity of a chartered accountant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return with four quarterly instalment payments during the fiscal year (for calendar-year taxpayers, due 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March of the following year) and a balancing payment due with the annual declaration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual IS return must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end. For a SARL whose fiscal year closes on 31 December, the return is due no later than the second working day following 1 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, registered name, SIREN/SIRET number, NAF/APE code, registered office address, and French tax identification number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must use its French legal entity identity. Non-resident beneficial ownership is not declared on the IS return; it is relevant only for withholding-tax relief filings and financial disclosure obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year, including the first fiscal year where a French SARL is newly registered or the period is shortened by corporate conversion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned SARL must compute the same fiscal-year period as its statutory accounts. No non-resident branch accounting period is permitted unless the entity itself is a French permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a – Revenue from principal commercial activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from patent prosecution, PCT filings, trademark registration, IP consultancy, official filing-fee billing and related agency services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue generated in France is reportable. Revenue from non-resident clients invoiced from France remains French-source income of the SARL; there is no automatic non-resident exemption merely because the client is abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1b – Other operating income and ancillary revenues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commissions, referral fees, translation reimbursements, official fee surcharges, annuity or maintenance fee billing, and all incidental operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned structures should not strip ancillary income through offshore invoicing without transfer-pricing documentation; substance and beneficial ownership of the revenue must remain in the French SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2a/2b – Operating expenses and cost of services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Personnel costs, professional fees, patent-office official fees, subscription fees to IP databases, office costs, depreciation, and amortisation of intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharges from foreign affiliates must be supported by invoices and a valid transfer-pricing analysis. Payment of licensing fees or head-office charges to a non-resident must satisfy the arm's-length principle and French thin-capitalisation rules where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 352/372 – Taxable result before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or deficit after adjusting the accounting result to the fiscal result, including deductibility limitations, IP patent-box election, depreciation recapture, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL with non-resident shareholders must apply the same adjustments. Dividend distributions or deemed distributions to shareholders are never deductible; payment of royalties for IP rights must respect beneficial-ownership conditions and patent-box eligibility.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 2065-SD attracts an automatic 10% increase of the net amount of IS due where the return is filed late or omitted; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month. A deliberate misstatement attracts a 40% penalty; an abuse of law or fraudulent manoeuvre attracts an 80% penalty; aggravated abuse of law may face a 100% penalty plus criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic law: 30% withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French tax-resident SARL to non-resident shareholders (Article 119 bis CGI). The statutory rate may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the non-resident corporate shareholder holds at least 5% of the SARL's capital for at least 24 months. Under many French tax treaties the applicable rate is 0%, 5% or 15%, depending on the shareholding percentage and the beneficial-ownership test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must provide a valid certificate of tax residence, usually Form 5000, issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction and submitted to the French paying company or withholding agent before the dividend payment date. The French withholding agent applies the treaty rate on the basis of the certificate; where the statutory 30% rate has already been levied, the shareholder may claim a refund through the French tax administration's DTA refund procedure. For EU parent-subsidiary relief, the parent must also meet the substantive holding and effective ownership conditions and provide the relevant French form 5057 / directive relief declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic statutory withholding tax of 33.33% on French-source patent royalties and similar industrial property remuneration paid to a non-resident, unless the applicable double tax treaty reduces the rate, commonly to 10% or 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for associated companies meeting the article's conditions. Interest: French domestic law generally does not subject arm's-length interest payments made by a French debtor to non-resident financial institutions or beneficial owners to withholding tax; a 25% withholding tax may apply to interest paid to entities established in non-cooperative states, and treaty rates or domestic exemptions apply where the beneficial owner proves entitlement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory French Local File and Master File documentation applies where the French taxpayer or the controlled group has annual turnover or gross balance-sheet assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where the French entity controls, or is controlled by, an entity abroad whose turnover or assets exceed the same threshold. Country-by-country reporting obligations arise for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulations filing regime comparable to the Gulf cooperation council ESR framework. However, French abuse-of-law doctrine, anti-hybrid rules, transfer-pricing rules and the Multilateral Instrument's Principal Purpose Test require a French IP prosecution SARL to demonstrate real economic substance: an office, employees, decision-making authority, board/governance meetings, bank accounts, accounting records and commercial activity in France. An IP-holding or patent-licensing structure using a hollow French SARL without substance is vulnerable to treaty denial, patent-box denial, recharacterisation and heavy penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing patent prosecution revenue, under-invoicing official filing fees, failing to report foreign client income, creating fictitious invoices for patent office expenses, or omitting distributed benefits from the IS return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment plus the 10% late filing penalty, 40% penalty for deliberate misdeclaration, 80% penalty for abuse of law and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud carries a sentence of up to five years' imprisonment and a criminal fine of up to EUR 500,000, with the fine capable of being doubled or increased to half the value of the concealed assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and de facto managers may be held personally liable for the SARL's tax debts and penalties where the fraud or management irregularity caused the company's insolvency or where assets were concealed in violation of tax collection rules. Courts may impose a travel ban, asset freezing, a prohibition from managing a company, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and artificial patent-holding arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a dormant SARL with no real employees, no physical presence, no active business conduct, and using it as a conduit to hold or license patents to an offshore affiliate to erode French taxable profits or claim an artificial patent-box benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax authority may invoke Article L.64 CGI abuse-of-law procedure to recharacterise the arrangement. An 80% abuse-of-law penalty applies to the undeclared tax, and a 100% penalty may apply where the taxpayer cannot show a non-tax purpose. The patent-box regime is denied retroactively and treaty benefits may be withdrawn under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate form is used solely as a sham, courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold the directors or shadow directors jointly and severally liable for the unpaid taxes, penalties and interest. Criminal sanctions, travel restrictions and disqualification orders may be imposed on individuals who knowingly used the shell structure to defraud the French Treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, retain, or file the French Local File, Master File or country-by-country report; cross-border payments to a foreign affiliate for management services, patent filing services or licensing without an arm's-length benchmark; providing incomplete documentation after a formal tax-authority request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the undocumented intra-group transaction, reassess profits using indirect methods, and shift the burden of proof to the taxpayer. Failure to produce the required transfer-pricing documentation can result in a fixed fine of EUR 10,000 per accounting year, and a 40% or 80% penalty if deliberate misstatements or fraudulent documentation are established. A transfer-pricing adjustment may also attract late-payment interest of 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false or incomplete documentation, or who cause the French entity to enter into non-arm's-length contracts for the purpose of tax evasion, may be made personally liable to the extent of the tax evaded under personal liability proceedings, and may face criminal fraud sanctions including fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and financial flows through shell bank accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an offshore payment account or Wise payment rails as a routing facility for client patent filing fees, mingling client funds with operating funds, issuing false invoices to repatriate funds disguised as professional fees, or knowingly receiving proceeds derived from predicate tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French anti-money-laundering rules impose reporting obligations, customer due-diligence requirements and record-keeping duties on relevant professionals. Failure to file a suspicious-transaction report with Tracfin may lead to administrative fines and criminal penalties; money laundering of tax fraud proceeds is punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 375,000, increased to EUR 1 million or more in sophisticated or organised cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors and beneficial owners can be prosecuted personally for AML violations. They may be subject to corporate-veil piercing, confiscation of assets, prohibition from managing commercial enterprises, travel bans and imprisonment. A pure corporate-veil defence is not available where the individual knowingly directed or benefited from the illicit flows.
